Due to available resources, all Phase II eligible (“awardable”) offeror(s) may not receive a proposal request, and not all requested proposals will result in an award. Submission of a WP does not guarantee advancement to Phase II (Request for Proposal), and the Government is under no obligation to make any award for solutions determined to be “awardable”. The Government reserves the right not to provide clarifications, or significant individual feedback, for submissions that do not advance. The Government will not include a comparison of submissions against a common statement of work (SOW) as the CFS provides no common SOW that constrain how interested parties must respond; instead, the WP represents a submission opportunity for a variety of innovative commercial items, technologies, and/or services that represent meaningful NGC2 modular capabilities of diverse scope and price. SECTION 2 – Problem Statement The NGC2 program is transitioning from prototyping at two operational units to the product delivery phase. While previous application efforts focused on experimentation, proof-of-concept development, and iterative development of application functionality, the next phase will emphasize the fielding of scalabl

rs transition among operational units every few years. As the NGC2 product delivery progresses, the Government will explore opportunities to find a balance between diversity and commonality in how applications are purchased and available to some or all of the Army. Consequently, the price for applications will account for purchasing for singular Army units (Division, Corps, Reserve) and purchasing for consumption-based usage (using application telemetry data to track how many users). The Government seeks to identify commercial solutions ready for operational product delivery and capable of supporting both current and emerging mission requirements. Solutions that successfully demonstrate technical merit, scalability, and affordability may be designated as awardable solutions, signifying that they can satisfy one or more anticipated Government capability needs. Once determined to be awardable, solutions are eligible for consideration for future acquisitions without requiring repeated technical evaluations, speeding up the acquisition timeline to meet emerging operational needs at pace. The objective is to reduce acquisition lead times, ensure applications are modular components with the data layer and accelerate the delivery of commercial capability to the warfighter. SECTION 3

SECTION 2 – Problem Statement The NGC2 program is transitioning from prototyping at two operational units to the product delivery phase. While previous application efforts focused on experimentation, proof-of-concept development, and iterative development of application functionality, the next phase will emphasize the fielding of scalable, mission-ready applications that comply with established architectural, cybersecurity, data, and interface standards. NGC2 applications cannot be standalone products; instead, they are productive interfaces for Warfighters to interact, visualize, and synthesize data in support of dynamic operations. Applications are not an end state for data. NGC2 applications provide a means to add context to data about the battlefield for rapid consumption by other users, algorithms, and/or AI agents. Data transformed by a user in an application must be published to the data layer, ensuring that it is discoverable and able to be consumed by any other applicable NGC2 component. The program is anticipating specifying the following performance requirements: reliability, maintainability, availability, latency, uplink success percentage1, and integrity for both the operational service and the monitoring service. Are there any other performance requirements that must be specified? b. The program is anticipating specifying the following functional requirements: coverage, routing and forwarding. Are there any other functional requirements that must be specified? c. The requirements for DDLS will mandate that movement and non-movement areas at 65 airports, the arrival and departure flows from these airports as well as CONUS Class A Airspace have coverage. Airport construction and airspace redesign will occur throughout the lifecycle of DDLS. How do you envision providing a network that responds to these changes without imposing financial shocks to the program based on change requests or that has inflated costs to manage the risk of occurrence? d. deliverables_scope.text: ===== FILE: files/Attachment_1_-_Salient_Characteristics.pdf ===== Salient Characteristics Document for PCB Prototyping System The requested equipment is required to support in-house rapid prototyping, milling, drilling, and routing of Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs). To meet mission requirements, submission must meet or exceed the physical, functional, and performance characteristics outlined below. 1. Essential Functional and Performance Characteristics • Milling Spindle Speed: Must be capable of reaching a maximum rotation speed of at least 60,000 RPM to process fine structures down to 100 µm. • Mechanical Resolution: Must offer a minimum resolution of 0.47 µm (0.02 mil) in the X/Y axes and 0.2 µm in the Z axis. • Repeatability: Must maintain a repeatability/precision tolerance of ± 5 µm (± 0.2 mil). • Tool Changing System: Must feature a fully automatic tool change mechanism capable of holding and cycling a minimum of 15

up to at least 305 mm x 229 mm x 8 mm (12" x 9" x 0.3"). • Maximum Material Size: Must physically accommodate substrates up to 330 mm x 250 mm x 26 mm (13" x 9.8" x 1"). • Base Construction: The machine must be built on a heavy granite (or equivalent high-density, vibration-dampening) base to ensure highest geometric accuracy and minimal resonance during 60,000 RPM operations. • Workholding: Must include an integrated vacuum table system for securing flexible and rigid substrates during the milling process. • Dispensing Capability: Must include or be capable of accepting a solder paste dispensing unit. 3. Operational & Software Requirements • Software Integration: Must include integrated CAM/system software capable of importing standard CAD data, managing material parameter libraries, and providing step-by-step process guidance. • Self-Cleaning: The spindle and milling depth sensor must feature pneumatic self-cleaning functionality to support low-maintenance operation. ===== FILE: files/FA301026Q0031.pdf ===== ===== FILE: files/sam_http_resources.json ===== { "notice_id": "1358ead4ca5342fcb912bb1e3d9e951b", "resources": [ { "resource_id": "d0335c968d104bf8a6bbfd0273cef3a8", "name": "Attachment 1 - Salient Characteristics

Project Purpose This project will replace native tree seedlings that were destroyed during a wildfire event affecting approximately 48 acres of the Refuge. The work is necessary to restore forest structure, stabilize soils, maintain habitat quality, and support long-term ecological recovery consistent with refuge management objectives. 2. Project Scope The Contractor shall provide all labor, equipment, seedlings, transportation, and materials to complete the following tasks. 2.1 Scope of Work • Supply bare-root seedlings of native species: o Persimmon, Chinkapin, Pecan, Bur oak, Pin oak, White oak, Swamp white oak, Northern red oak, and Shagbark hickory. • Seedlings must be sourced from suppliers using local native seed stock approved by the Refuge. • Plant approximately 22,050 seedlings across 48 acres at 10 ft x 10 ft spacing. • Use a tractor-mounted planting machine suitable for penetrating compacted soils. • Ensure proper planting technique that maintains good root -to-soil contact. • Keep all seedlings moist, shaded, and chilled before and during planting. • Avoid any ground disturbance beyond the depth or are

rmed as per the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 25, Standard for Inspections, Testing, and Maintenance of Water-Based Fire Protection Systems and all other associated NFPA Standards. This is considered a remote location, and connectivity can be an issue. Background YOSE has over 138 fire suppression systems in buildings parkwide. Each system is inspected each year and deficiencies identified. This project is to bring the fire suppression systems in the El Portal Residences known as the Motor Inn Cabins, Yosemite Valley residences, Wawona District residences, and Mather District residences into compliance with NFPA requirements. This project encompasses a total of 40 locations and represents 43 individual fire suppression systems. The contractor will perform tasks to rectify the fire suppression system deficiencies identified during the annual inspections. Deficiencies include the following, but not limited to interval testing, replace missing signage, replacing air and water gauges, installing electric bells, replacing recalled sprinkler heads, adding wrenches and heads for head boxes, replacing painted sprinkler heads, adjustment of water flow switches, and performing system inspections with passing reports.
